international.title: EU leaders brace for tough talks on budget and Ukraine – Europe live
international.summary: António Costa says the next long-term budget is ‘the most important’ item on the agenda Latvia’s Andris Kulbergs offered a similar argument, saying that countries on the eastern flank had to ramp up their defence spending, often at the cost of other priorities, and so need to be supported with a strong EU budget with funds for cohesion and agriculture. “We are putting the most money in security and defence, as we are getting attacked as an economy [because of] geographical punishment, but then we are seeing in our shops all these products from countries getting the most support of farmers. … That is not really the case of free trade, and that’s exactly where we need that support,” he said. “They should not … be in a position [that they need] to take a bad deal.” Continue reading...
